item.title: Daniel Moriarty scholarship applications now open
item.description: KILAUEA — The Friends of Kauai Wildlife Refuges, the nonprofit friends group that provides support to the Kauai National Wildlife Refuge Complex, announced that the nonprofit is currently accepting applications for their annual scholarship in honor of Daniel Moriarty.

item.title: EDITORIAL: Turtle Bay tests land-use conflicts
item.description: Environmental and community groups represented by lawyers with Earthjustice filed suit Tuesday, challenging plans for a new hotel at Turtle Bay on Oahu’s North Shore. The suit charges that Maryland- based Host Hotels & Resorts and Honolulu’s Department of Planning and Permitting (DPP) relied on an outdated environmental report, and failed to take into account a newly listed endangered species of bees and evolving ecological conditions.

item.title: Credit unions look to make taxes easier
item.description: LIHUE — The Finance Department has created a new partnership with five local credit unions to make paying real property taxes easier and more convenient for residents.

item.title: State soccer champs moved to Wednesday
item.description: HONOLULU — The Hawaii High School Athletic Association (HHSAA) announced the rescheduling of final-day matches for the 2026 Boys Soccer Division I and Division II Soccer State Championships on Saturday.

item.title: Long-vacant state jobs with languishing funds on rise in Hawaii
item.description: The number of stagnant state job vacancies tying up taxpayer revenue jumped last year after flattening in 2024, expanding a pile of cash that some Hawaii lawmakers want to use for urgent needs amid looming budget uncertainties.

item.title: Hiker rescued on Kalalau Trail Friday
item.description: LIHUE — Personnel from the Kauai Fire Department rescued a 27-year-old male visitor from New York on the Kalalau Trail Wednesday, with an apparent ankle injury.

item.title: Green’s tax cut freeze plan repeals five years of additional savings for taxpayers
item.description: Hawaii taxpayers stand to receive dramatically stunted financial savings under a plan by Gov. Josh Green to cancel future state income tax cuts.

item.title: State parks closed due to weather
item.description: HONOLULU — As of Sunday, Feb. 8, 2026, at 3 p.m., the Hawaii State Department of Land and Natural Resources (DLNR) closed all state parks and forest areas to the public due to the expected continuance of severe weather conditions across the state.

item.title: Officials advise avoiding travel; refuge shelters on standby
item.description: LIHUE — County of Kauai officials are urging the public to stay home, avoid all unnecessary travel, and prioritize safety as severe weather conditions continued Sunday and are expected to last into this week.

item.title: Abalos wins the Kauai Complex Area Spelling Bee
item.description: LIHUE — Twenty students representing schools from around the island participated in the 2026 Kauai Complex Area Spelling Bee at the Chiefess Kamakahelei Middle School cafeteria Friday night, continuing the tradition of welcoming Super Bowl weekend.
